title: Electrospinning Growth Factor Releasing Microspheres into Fibrous Scaffolds
protocol: Prepare 2% w/v polyvinyl alcohol (PVA) solution in deionized water.
Stir the 2% PVA solution at 50 °C until clear.
Prepare 0.5% w/v PVA solution in deionized water.
Stir the 0.5% PVA solution at 50 °C until clear.
Prepare a solution of 2% v/v Isopropyl Alcohol in deionized water.
Dissolve 300 mg of 65:35 poly(lactic-co-glycolic acid) (PLGA) in 3 ml of Dichloromethane using a vortex mixer to accelerate dissolution.
Combine 200 µl of protein solution with 4 µl of 2% PVA solution.
Pour the protein mixture into the PLGA solution.
Place the tube containing the protein and PLGA mixture into a beaker of ice water.
Agitate the solution using a wand sonicator at ~10 Watts (RMS) for a few seconds until a uniform creamy white emulsion is created.
Pour the emulsion into 40 ml of the prepared 0.5% PVA solution in a 50 ml centrifuge tube.
Mix the emulsion and 0.5% PVA solution at high speed on a vortex mixer for ~20 sec until the solution develops a cloudy appearance.
Transfer the emulsion to a 200 ml beaker and place on a stir plate at 350 rpm for 2 min.
Add 50 ml of 2% isopropyl alcohol to the beaker on the stir plate.
Allow the mixture to continue stirring for a minimum of 1 hr to allow the DCM to evaporate and the PLGA to harden.
Transfer the microsphere solution into centrifuge tubes.
Centrifuge at 425 x g for 3 min.
Carefully remove the supernatant from the tube, above the microspheres, and store in a 500 ml bottle.
Rinse the microspheres with deionized water by filling the tube three quarters full and shaking it to redistribute the microspheres in the liquid.
Repeat steps rinsing the microspheres four times.
Remove the supernatant again after the final rinse and place in the 500 ml bottle with other samples.
Freeze the microspheres collected in the centrifuge tube.
Lyophilize for at least 24 hr.
Visualize the microspheres under a light microscope or with a Scanning Electron Microscope.
Store the dried microspheres in a -20 °C freezer.
Create a 0.5% w/v solution of photoinitiator in deionized water by dissolving at 37 °C.
Dissolve PEO in deionized water at 90% of the final volume desired.
Stir the dissolved PEO mixture using a heated stir plate or water bath at 37 °C to accelerate dissolution if necessary.
Add MeHA to the stirred PEO solution and use a vortex mixer to stir until clear.
Add the 0.5% photo initiator solution to fill the remaining 10% volume of the desired final electrospinning solution.
Add microspheres to the solution at the desired concentration up to 400 mg/ml.
Mix the solution on a vortex mixer until the microspheres are evenly distributed.
Transfer the mixed solution to a syringe and attach a 6 inch 18 gauge blunt tip needle.
Place the syringe in a syringe pump and set it to dispense at 1.2 ml/hr.
Tape a layer of aluminum foil on the collection plate or mandrel.
Connect the ground wire from a high voltage power source to the collection apparatus.
Connect the positive lead to the needle.
Adjust the syringe pump and collection surface so that there is 15 cm between the needle tip and collection surface.
Start the polymer pumping when the solution is visible at the end of the syringe.
Turn on the voltage source and set the voltage to 24 kV.
Run the solution until the desired scaffold thickness is achieved.
Turn off the voltage source and syringe pump when complete.
Remove foil with the attached scaffold.
Store completed scaffolds containing protein in a -20 °C freezer.
Prepare cell culture media by adding 10% v/v Fetal Bovine Serum, 1% v/v L-Glutamine, and 1% v/v Penicillin-Streptomycin to Dulbecco’s Modified Eagle’s Medium.
Select glass coverslips that fit completely into a well plate.
Treat the coverslips with 3-(Trimethoxysilyl)propyl methacrylate as described by the manufacturer.
Attach methacrylated coverslips to the collection area of the electrospinner with removable double-sided tape.
Electrospin to desired thickness as described above.
Carefully remove coverslips from mandrel after electrospinning.
Place scaffold-coated coverslips into a clear nitrogen chamber and purge all oxygen.
Expose the chamber and scaffold to a 10 mW/cm² 365 nm light for 15 min.
After crosslinking, place scaffolds into appropriately sized well plates with the scaffold side facing up.
Sterilize scaffolds under a germicidal lamp for 30 min.
If desired, coat scaffolds with fibronectin or other protein as per manufacturer’s instructions to enhance cell adhesion.
Harvest Dorsal Root Ganglia (DRG) as previously described.
Place 100-200 μl of media on each scaffold in the well plate.
Carefully place one DRG on each scaffold in the media droplet.
Incubate the scaffold and DRG at 37 °C for 4 hr to allow cells to adhere.
Fill the media to the appropriate level for the well and place back into the incubator.
Continue incubating for 4-6 days.
Carefully remove the media from each well after the incubation period.
Gently wash once with PBS.
Fix cells for 30 min using 4% w/v paraformaldehyde.
Stain cells using an antibody stain for neurofilament.
Visualize nuclei of the cells using DAPI.
Locate the cell mass using the filter and excitation settings for DAPI.
Switch the filter to FITC to visualize extended neurites.
Collect and combine images as necessary to see the entire structure using the stitch function on the microscope.
